title: Streaming: graceful client shutdown, resumable checkpoints, and client-side metrics for Go SDK
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement: Go SDK streaming APIs today expose a low-level Reader/Iterator pattern for server-sent tokens but lack a recommended, ergonomic approach for graceful client-initiated shutdown when a context deadline is hit, and for capturing per-session progress metrics. In practice apps need: (1) a clear contract for best-effort flush/close so partial responses are usable, (2) an optional resumable checkpoint token model to continue long-running streams after transient cancellations, and (3) client-side metrics (tokens emitted, latency to first token, bytes streamed, abort reason) wired into Redwood Console.

Goals: 1) Define an ergonomic Go API that composes with context.Context and makes it easy to do graceful shutdown vs. hard abort; 2) Implement client-side checkpointing support (optional token echo) and resume path that is safe for at-most-once semantics where possible; 3) Emit structured client-side metrics and attach a session_id to correlate with server traces; 4) Add integration tests and a small example app demonstrating cancel-to-resume flow; 5) Provide migration docs and rollout plan.

Success criteria (measurable):
- API landed that passes Go linters and has idiomatic usage example in README.
- Benchmark: average tail-latency (end-to-end) stays within 10% of baseline for common short streams (< 2s) and improves perceived availability for long streams when using resumable checkpoints.
- Observability: session metrics appear in Console test org within 24h of rollout and show tokens/latency per session.
- Integration tests cover: immediate cancel, deadline cancel, resumed session, server abort and client retry behavior.

Design notes / trade-offs: 
- API ergonomics: expose StreamSession struct with methods: Next(ctx), CloseWithReason(ctx, reason string), Checkpoint() -> optional token, Resume(ctx, token). We considered adding context-derived deadlines only (no CloseWithReason) but CloseWithReason helps surface intent and maps to server-side metrics.
- Checkpoint size and privacy: checkpoint is opaque string from server; server decides how much state to encode. We keep it optional to avoid adding cost to every short-lived request.
- Semantics: resume is best-effort and provides at-least-once for output fragments after last confirmed checkpoint; clients must deduplicate at application layer if exact once is required. Documented clearly.
- Backpressure & deadlines: Next(ctx) honors ctx cancellation immediately; when ctx times out we attempt a single best-effort CloseWithReason("deadline") call to server; if CloseWithReason cannot complete within 100ms we return to caller with context error. This balances latency SLOs vs. server cleanup.
- Resource cleanup: session goroutine guarantees KV cache handles and stream sockets are closed within 500ms of client CloseWithReason returning; otherwise runtime will leak and be flagged.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) API sketch and public godoc (PR #TBD).
2) Implement StreamSession wrapper around existing stream Reader in go-sdk; wire session_id generation (uuid v4) and attach to headers.
3) Checkpointing: implement optional Checkpoint() that requests a token from server; wire to wire protocol with new header X-Resume-Token. Runtime-side stub exists (ENG-900900) but needs minor compatibility.
4) Metrics: add client-only metrics via telemetry package: label session_id, tokens_emitted, first_token_latency_ms, abort_reason. Hook to internal telemetry pipeline used by Console.
5) Tests: unit tests for semantics, e2e test against local runtime shim that simulates partial output and supports resume.
6) Example app: streaming-transcribe example demonstrating cancel/resume and a small tutorial in README.
7) Docs + migration guide; feature gate behind runtime-compat flag in SDK config (default enabled once runtime is rolled out).

Acceptance criteria:
- PR merged with CI green and 5 reviewers sign-off (eng + pm + docs).
- E2E tests pass in CI with runtime shim.
- Console shows sample session metrics in staging org.

Risks:
- Resume semantics might be misunderstood by customers (we mitigate with docs, example apps, and explicit server token opaqueness).
- Server/Runtime dependency: requires runtime support for resume tokens; currently blocked until runtime stubs are merged (ENG-900900).
- Potential privacy exposure if checkpoint encoded user prompt fragments — server team must ensure tokens are safe.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated default off in minor release (go-sdk-0.43.0-feature-gated).
- Internal dogfood in Redwood apps for 2 weeks.
- Enable in beta for select customers (PM-led).
- Gradual enable for all once runtime compatibility confirmed and Console metrics verified.

Follow-ups:
- UX: propose a small change to Console to show resumable session count and resume success rate.
- SDK: extend pattern to TypeScript and Python, and unify semantics.
